correctness.rationale: The conditional row-selection identity is exact; polar coordinates separate the simultaneous-zero radial threshold q<md from the single-zero-row angular threshold q<d+2s. Positive Gaussian density at zero provides matching divergence witnesses. Noncentral chi-square Poisson mixing gives the exact second moment; independent gamma-beta factorization gives central all-q moments. The accompanying reproduction program was executed against numerical quadrature and sampled updates. No empirical result replaces the infinite-moment proof.

value.rationale: The sharp and complete moment-existence phase diagram identifies when observed row-norm weighting regularizes the inverse row-length singularity, yet exposes a competing simultaneous-zero-matrix singularity. It rigorously distinguishes uniform from classical norm-weighted row choices in dimensions one and two, supplies an exact noncentral mean-square formula for arbitrary true designs, and proves finite Gaussian observation averaging cannot cure a divergent moment. These are material robustness boundaries for low-dimensional doubly noisy row-action solvers, not merely a recalculation of a fixed-matrix contraction bound.
